clipper.keywords: clipper clip hard clip soft clip knee oversampling anti-aliasing ceiling peak loudness drums 808 mastering saturation parallel
slider_desc: Gain into the clipper (-12 to +24 dB): the more you push, the more of each peak is shaved off at the Ceiling.
The level the clipper never passes (-24 to 0 dB); the default -0.1 dB keeps a hair of headroom below full scale.
Shape of the corner: 0% is a hard clip, higher values bend the top of the wave smoothly into the Ceiling (100% = a full soft tanh curve).
Runs the clipper at 2x, 4x or 8x the sample rate so the harmonics it creates do not fold back as aliasing (Off = no latency, more grit).
Blend of clipped and dry signal (the dry path is delayed to match), for parallel clipping.
Level after the mix (-24 to +12 dB).
Stereo applies the same gain to both channels so the image stays put; Dual clips each channel on its own.
uses: Shave drum transients on a bus for more level without a limiter's pumping
Smash 808s and kicks into a dense, loud low end
Catch the last peaks before a limiter on the master for extra loudness
Add soft saturation and glue with a high Knee and some Mix
Parallel clipping for punch that keeps the dry transients
clipper.properties: Signal chain: Input gain → optional oversampling (1 to 3 linear-phase halfband FIR stages, 63/23/15 taps, Kaiser-windowed sinc) → clipper: linear up to Ceiling × (1 − Knee), then a tanh bend into the Ceiling (Knee 0 = hard clip), linked or per channel → back down → Mix with the delayed dry signal → Output. Latency 0 / 31 / 37 / 39 samples (Off / 2x / 4x / 8x), reported for delay compensation. With oversampling the band-limited output can peak slightly above Ceiling.

de_plosive.keywords: de-plosive deplosive plosive pop p b pops vocal voice dialogue podcast mic thump low end burst repair restoration
slider_desc: How easily a burst counts as a plosive: the low band must jump above the high band and its own average by 12 dB at 0% down to 0 dB at 100% (6 dB at the default 50%).
Crossover frequency (60 to 400 Hz): only the band below it is detected and turned down.
The most the low band is turned down during a plosive (0 to 30 dB).
How fast the low band comes back after the pop (20 to 300 ms).
On outputs only what is being removed, to hear exactly what the detector catches.
uses: Remove P and B pops from close-miked vocals
Clean plosives from podcasts, voice-over and dialogue
Tame thumps from handheld mics and stand bumps
Fix pops after recording without a high-pass that thins the whole voice
de_plosive.properties: Signal chain: Linkwitz-Riley 24 dB/oct crossover at Frequency (sums back flat) → detector on both channels: fast low- and high-band envelopes (1 ms / 30 ms) and a slow low-band average (200 ms); when the low band rises above both by more than the threshold it is cut by twice the excess, up to Max Reduction (1 ms attack, Release) → bands summed. Both bands run 5 ms late (look-ahead) so the onset is caught; that latency is reported for delay compensation. Only the low band is ever changed.

The step clock follows the host tempo and, while the transport plays, is read from the song position; stopped it free-runs at the tempo (120 BPM without one). Every change of effect crossfades over 4 ms, so steps switch without clicks. Fully deterministic, zero latency; MIDI passes through.

tape_echo.keywords: tape echo space echo multi-head delay repeat dub reggae spring reverb wow flutter saturation self-oscillation runaway vintage analog tempo sync freeze
slider_desc: Time between the record head and playback head 1 (50 to 1000 ms); heads 2 and 3 sit at twice and three times this distance. A change glides like a tape motor, so the echoes bend in pitch.
Locks head 1 to a note at the project tempo (straight, dotted or triplet); heads 2 and 3 follow at 2x and 3x. Off uses Repeat Time.
The classic 12-position selector: which playback heads you hear and feed back (1, 2, 3 and their combinations), the R positions add the spring reverb, and R alone is the reverb without echoes.
Feedback of the active heads into one shared loop; 100% is unity loop gain in every mode, above it the echo runs away into self-oscillation that the tape saturation keeps bounded.
Low shelf at 250 Hz on the echoes (-12 to +12 dB).
High shelf at 2.5 kHz on the echoes (-12 to +12 dB).
Tape wow (two slow sines, up to 2.5 ms) and flutter (two fast sines, up to 0.15 ms) moving every head together, so the repeats waver in pitch.
Tape drive inside the feedback loop: 0% only rounds very loud repeats, higher values squash and colour every repeat with asymmetric (even) harmonics.
Level of the spring reverb, heard in the R positions of the Heads selector; it is fed with the input and the echoes.
Blend between the dry signal and the echoes (plus the spring).
Stops recording and loops what is on the tape (the length of the longest active head) forever, without fading or building up.
uses: Dub and reggae echoes that build and run away under your hand
Rhythmic multi-head patterns from one repeat time
Slapback with tape colour on vocals and guitars
Spring-drenched surf and ambient washes in the R modes
Warbly lo-fi delays with heavy wow, flutter and saturation
tape_echo.properties: Signal chain: Input + loop → stereo tape (record head) → playback heads at 1x, 2x, 3x the repeat time (4-point Hermite reads, wow/flutter on all heads, the time glides over ~0.12 s) → heads of the selected mode summed → feedback loop: ÷ number of heads → 12 dB/oct low-pass at 4.5 kHz → asymmetric soft saturation (slope 1 at 0, bounded) → 90 Hz one-pole low cut → × Intensity back onto the tape. Echo output: heads ÷ √(number of heads) → Bass (low shelf 250 Hz) → Treble (high shelf 2.5 kHz) → + spring tank in the R modes (two dispersive 40-stage all-pass springs, 2.2 s decay, fed with input and echoes) → Dry/Wet Mix. Tape length 6.75 s (3 × a dotted quarter at 40 bpm); zero latency.

wah.keywords: wah wah-wah pedal auto-wah autowah envelope filter quack funk guitar bass keys clavinet lfo sweep vocal formant talk band-pass resonant tempo sync
slider_desc: Pedal position from heel (0%) to toe (100%) in Manual mode, smoothed over 15 ms; automate it or map a MIDI CC to it.
Manual: the Pedal slider moves the filter. Auto: an envelope follower moves it with your playing dynamics. LFO: a smooth sweep at Rate or in time with the project.
Classic: the inductor wah's narrow peak from about 400 Hz to 2.2 kHz. Vocal: two formant peaks that move together like a vowel changing. Wide: a broader sweep from 200 Hz to 3.5 kHz.
Sharpness and height of the peak: more Resonance gives a narrower, louder, more vocal quack.
Auto mode: how loud you must play to reach the toe, from 0 dBFS at 0% down to -42 dBFS at 100% (the pedal moves over the 30 dB below that).
Auto mode: how fast the envelope follower opens the filter (1 to 100 ms).
Auto mode: how fast the filter falls back after a note (20 to 1000 ms).
LFO mode: sweeps per second when Tempo Sync is off (0.1 to 10 Hz).
LFO mode: one full sweep per note at the project tempo (1/1 to 1/16), locked to the bar while the transport plays.
Blend between the dry signal and the wah.
Level after the wah (-12 to +12 dB) to match the bypassed level.
uses: Classic wah on guitar, automated or played from a MIDI expression pedal
Funky auto-wah (envelope filter) on clean guitar, bass and clavinet
Tempo-synced wah rhythms on chords and synths
Talking vowel sweeps with the Vocal model
A fixed half-cocked pedal for a nasal lead tone
wah.properties: Signal chain: pedal position (Manual: smoothed slider; Auto: peak envelope follower with Attack/Release mapped over 30 dB below the Sensitivity level; LFO: raised cosine at Rate or one cycle per note, beat-locked while playing) → exponential frequency curve per model → TPT state-variable band-pass (Q 2-10 Classic, 3-10 Vocal with a second formant at 0.7 level, 1.2-6.2 Wide), normalised to 0 dB peak and lifted by +3.5 to +9.5 dB with Resonance → Dry/Wet Mix → Output. The filter is modulated every sample; zero latency.

half_speed.keywords: half speed halftime half-time slow down octave down tempo sync bar grid time stretch granular pitch keep drop transition creative dubstep trap
slider_desc: How much input is captured per cycle: a 1/4 or 1/2 note, 1 Bar or 2 Bars at the host tempo.
Playback speed of the captured audio: 1/2 is classic halftime (an octave down), 1/4 a quarter speed (two octaves down), 2/3 a lazier drag; one cycle lasts Length / Speed.
Off slows the audio like a tape (lower pitch); On uses overlapping 40 ms grains so only the tempo halves and the pitch stays the same.
High cut on the slowed signal (1 to 20 kHz) to tame the dull or grainy top end; 20 kHz is off.
Blend of slowed and dry signal.
Shifts the cycle start by 0 to 3 beats from the bar line while the transport plays.
uses: Instant halftime drops and breakdowns on drums or full mixes
Octave-down slowed-tape textures on vocals and synths
Quarter-speed drones and pads from any loop
Pitch-kept halftime grooves that stay in key
Transitions that drag the beat before the next section
half_speed.properties: Signal chain: Input → cycle buffer (one cycle = Length / Speed; the first Length of each cycle is recorded) → read from the cycle start at Speed (linear interpolation) or, with Pitch Keep, two Hann grains of ~40 ms half a grain apart that follow the slowed read point at the original pitch → 5 ms crossfade at every new cycle → one-pole high cut (Tone) → Mix with the dry signal → Output. While the transport plays, the cycle is locked to the song position (bar line + Sync Offset); stopped, it free-runs at the host tempo (40 to 300 bpm). No latency is reported: the slowed output is a musical effect, not a delay to compensate.

slicer.keywords: slicer beat slicer slice rearrange shuffle stutter reverse backspin random beat repeat chop remix loop glitch breakbeat tempo sync bar grid
slider_desc: How the previous bar's slices are rearranged: Straight keeps the order, Shuffle swaps the picked slices among themselves, Reverse Pairs plays picked pairs backwards as one piece, Stutter repeats the slice before, Backspin rewinds the audio like a turntable, Random plays any slice.
Chance that each slice is picked by the Pattern (0% = the bar plays in order, 100% = every slice is changed).
Number that sets every random choice (1 to 999): the same Seed always gives the same pattern, and it stays the same every bar.
How many equal slices the bar is cut into: 8 (eighth notes), 16 (sixteenths) or 32.
Chance that a slice plays backwards.
Chance that a slice is retriggered, playing its first half twice.
Length of each slice (100% = full); lower values cut every slice short with a fade for a choppy, gated feel.
Blend of sliced and dry signal.
uses: Live breakbeat-style rearrangements of drum loops
Stutter and repeat fills at the end of a phrase
Reversed and backspun variations of vocals and synth lines
Choppy gated rhythms from pads and chords
Repeatable random remixes: change the Seed until one grooves
slicer.properties: Signal chain: Input → two bar buffers (4 beats at the host tempo, one recording while the other plays) → previous bar cut into 8/16/32 slices → slice order and per-slice reverse, repeat (first half twice) and backspin from Pattern, Variation and the chances, all drawn from a Park-Miller generator seeded by Seed → Gate shortens each slice → 2.5 ms fades at every cut (slices that continue the audio seamlessly are not faded) → Mix with the dry signal → Output. The output runs one bar behind (a musical delay, not reported as latency); until the first bar is recorded the input passes through. While the transport plays the bar is locked to the song position; stopped, it free-runs at the host tempo (40 to 300 bpm, 4/4).

slider_desc: Picks the transfer curve: Soft, Hard, Tube, Fold, Sine, Steps and Asym are built in, Custom uses the eight points below (in the GFX and VST3/CLAP interfaces, picking a shape copies its points and dragging one switches to Custom).

Output of curve point 2 (-1 to +1) for that input; values below the previous points fold the wave back.

Output of curve point 7 (-1 to +1) for that input; values below the previous points fold the wave back.
Input position of curve point 8 (0 to 1 of full scale; 0 leaves the point unused), read when Shape is Custom.
Output of curve point 8 (-1 to +1) for that input; values below the previous points fold the wave back.

Warm up bass, synths or drums with soft tube-like saturation and a little bias
Fold basslines and leads into rich, metallic overtones

Parallel distortion with Mix, tamed by the Tone low-pass
shaper.properties: Signal chain: Drive gain → optional oversampling (1 or 2 linear-phase halfband FIR stages, 63/23 taps, as in Clipper) → Bias offset → the transfer curve: (0, 0) plus up to 8 points joined by monotone cubic (PCHIP) segments, sampled into a 1024-step table read with linear interpolation, flat after the last point and above full scale, mirrored for negative input (or a fixed gentler curve in Asymmetric) → back down → 10 Hz DC blocker → Tone (12 dB/oct low-pass, off at 20 kHz) → Mix with the delayed dry signal → Output. Latency 0 / 31 / 37 samples (Off / 2x / 4x), reported for delay compensation.

draw_eq.card_desc: EQ You Draw with Ten Points
draw_eq.keywords: draw eq drawable equalizer curve graphic eq 10 band ten band octave smooth tone shaping tilt smile air low end mud telephone spectrum analyzer mix
slider_desc: Gain at 31 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): the sub and deep low end; drag the first point in the curve.
Gain at 63 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): kick and bass weight.
Gain at 125 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): bass body and warmth.
Gain at 250 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): low mids, where mud and boxiness build up.
Gain at 500 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): body of voices, guitars and snares.
Gain at 1 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): the centre of the midrange, nasal or honky when boosted.
Gain at 2 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): presence and attack.
Gain at 4 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): clarity and edge, harsh if pushed.
Gain at 8 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): brilliance and sibilance.
Gain at 16 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): air and sparkle (left out at sample rates below 36 kHz).
How smoothly the curve flows between the points (0 to 100%): low values give each point its own defined bump, high values blend them into broad, gentle slopes.
Level after the EQ (-18 to +18 dB), to match loudness after big boosts or cuts.
Blend of equalized and dry signal (0 to 100%), for subtle or parallel tone shaping.
uses: Sketch a tone curve by dragging across the display instead of setting bands one by one
Gentle tilts and smiles on a mix bus or master
Carve mud and add air on vocals, guitars and pads
Telephone and old radio voices with steep cuts at both ends
Match a reference by drawing against the live spectrum behind the curve
draw_eq.properties: Ten points at fixed octave-spaced frequencies (31.25 Hz to 16 kHz) set the gain the curve passes through. Each point drives an RBJ peaking filter; the ten gains are solved (Gaussian elimination on the filters' interaction, then two corrections with the true response) so the cascade passes through every point to within a fraction of a dB, and Smoothness sets the filters' Q from 1.5 to 0.6. Minimum-phase IIR, zero latency; with every point at 0 dB the filters are bypassed and the plugin is transparent. Mix with the dry signal, then Output. The GFX and VST3/CLAP interfaces draw the response over a live output spectrum: drag across the display to draw, double-click a point to reset it.

phase_align.keywords: phase align alignment polarity invert flip delay time align all-pass allpass phase rotation rotator correlation meter multi-mic drums kick in out snare top bottom bass di amp sidechain reference mono compatibility
slider_desc: What is aligned to what: Right to Left moves the right channel against the left, Track to Sidechain moves the track against a reference on channels 3/4 (reports a fixed 10 ms latency so it can also move the track earlier).
How late the moved signal plays (-10 to +10 ms); negative values make it earlier (in Right to Left the left channel is delayed instead).
Sub-sample fine tuning of the delay (-1 to +1 samples), for alignment the millisecond steps cannot reach.
Flips the polarity of the left channel (of the track's left channel in Sidechain mode).
Flips the polarity of the right channel (of the track's right channel in Sidechain mode).
Turns the phase of the moved signal by this angle at the Focus frequency (0 to 360 degrees; 0 and 360 = off), for low end that a time shift alone cannot line up.
The frequency where Rotation is exact (20 to 1000 Hz): set it to the fundamental that matters, such as the kick or bass note.
Mono Sum plays the moved signal added to its reference, so you can hear when the two are fullest together; Normal plays the result.
uses: Line up kick in and kick out, or snare top and bottom mics
Align a bass DI with its amp or cabinet mic
Check and fix polarity on multi-mic recordings
Undo a Haas delay or fix a stereo pair recorded with a timing offset
Turn the phase of a bass under a kick until the low end adds up
phase_align.properties: Delay line per channel with whole-sample exact reads and 4-point Catmull-Rom interpolation for fractions; per-channel polarity; Rotation by two first-order all-pass filters, each turning half the angle at Focus (less below it, more above). Right to Left needs no latency: a negative delay delays the left channel instead. Track to Sidechain delays the track by ceil(10 ms) + 1 samples less the delay and reports that as latency, so the track can also move ahead of the reference; the reference is only listened to (Mono Sum) and metered. The GFX and VST3/CLAP interfaces show the phase difference across frequency, the total delay, the latency and the correlation of the two signals (full band and below 150 Hz). In REAPER, send the reference to channels 3/4 of the track.

slider_desc: Chord plays a chord on every key; Progression lets the white keys from C play the steps of the chosen chord progression.
The key the chords (or the progression) are in.

The scale the chords are built from in Chord mode (major, minor, harmonic or melodic minor and the modes); a key outside it plays the chord of the scale note below. Progression mode uses the progression's own major or minor.
What every key plays: a triad, a 7th or 9th chord stacked in the scale, a sus2 or sus4 chord, or a power chord (root, fifth, octave).
Moves the lowest notes of the chord up an octave: root position, first, second or third inversion.
Spreads the chord: Close keeps it within an octave, Drop 2 drops the second-highest note an octave, Open lifts every other note, Wide also drops the bass an octave.
Moves every chord up or down by octaves (-2 to +2).
Plays the notes of each chord one after another, this far apart (0 to 200 ms), like a strummed guitar or a harp; notes not yet played when the key is released are skipped.
The order of the strum: upward, downward, or alternating with every chord.
Shapes the velocity of the chord notes: positive values play soft touches louder, negative values make them softer (0% passes it unchanged).

The chord progression of Progression mode: C, D, E, F, G, A and B play its steps in turn (I-V-vi-IV, I-vi-IV-V, vi-IV-I-V, I-IV-vi-V, ii-V-I, Pachelbel's Canon, i-VI-III-VII, i-VII-VI-V and i-iv-V-i).
uses: Play full chords with one finger on any MIDI instrument, always in key
Sketch songs fast: the white keys play a whole progression in any key
Rich 7th and 9th voicings with Drop 2 or Open for keys and pads
Strummed guitar-like chords or harp rolls from a single key
Power chords for rock and synth leads
chords.properties: A MIDI effect: MIDI in, MIDI out, the audio passes through untouched (place it before an instrument). Chords are stacked in thirds inside the scale (sus2/sus4 swap the third for the second or fourth), then inverted, voiced, moved by octaves and kept within 0 to 127. Every note-on sent is remembered with the key that made it, so the key's release always ends exactly those notes, whatever was changed meanwhile; strum notes still waiting are dropped; a note two keys share sounds until both are released; all notes off (CC 120/123) releases every key of its channel. Pitch bend, controllers and sustain pass through; poly pressure goes to every note of the key's chord. Sample-accurate and the same in the JSFX, the GFX version and the VST3/CLAP.

The scale every note is fitted to: major, natural, harmonic or melodic minor, the modes (Dorian to Locrian), major or minor pentatonic, or blues.

How a note outside the scale is fixed: moved to the Nearest scale note (ties go down), always Up or always Down, dropped (Filter), or White Keys, where C, D, E, F, G, A and B play the scale's degrees from the key and the black keys are silent.
Moves the incoming notes by semitones before they are fitted to the scale, so the result stays in key (in White Keys mode it moves what the keys play).

uses: Never hit a wrong note: every key snaps into the song's key
Play any scale on the white keys alone, in any key
Clean up MIDI from a controller or a pitch-to-MIDI converter
Drop out-of-key notes from generated or recorded parts
Quick transposition and octave shifts that stay in key
scale.properties: A MIDI effect: MIDI in, MIDI out, the audio passes through untouched (place it before an instrument). Every note is mapped once, when it starts; its note-off always ends the very note that was sent, even when the settings change while it is held, and a note two keys share sounds until both are released. All notes off (CC 120/123) releases every key of its channel; pitch bend, controllers, sustain and pressure pass through (poly pressure follows the mapped note). slider_desc: The length of each step, locked to the tempo: 1/4 to 1/32 notes, with dotted (D) and triplet (T) values.
The order the held notes play in: Up, Down, Up-Down, Down-Up, in the order they were played, Random, or Chord (all notes on every step).
How many octaves the pattern climbs through (1 to 4): the held notes, then the same notes an octave up, and so on.
How long each note sounds, as a share of its step (5 to 200%): short values give staccato plucks, 100% is legato, above 100% the notes overlap.
Moves every second step later (0 to 100%) for a shuffle feel; 100% is a full triplet swing.
On: the arpeggio keeps playing after you let go of the keys, until you play a new chord. Off: it stops when the last key is released.

arpeggiator.properties: A MIDI effect: MIDI in, MIDI out, the audio passes through untouched (place it before an instrument). Steps fall on a grid locked to the host's beat position while it plays (a held chord starts on the next step); while it is stopped the arpeggio runs at the tempo from the first key. The sequence is the held notes by pitch (or as played) over the octaves; each step plays one note, or every note for Chord, for Gate % of the step, with the played velocity times the step's lane value. Every note sent is ended: releasing the last key (without Latch), all notes off (CC 120/123) and the transport stopping end the arpeggio's notes at once; a pitch played twice in a row starts again cleanly. Controllers, pitch bend and other messages pass through. The Random pattern uses an exact Park-Miller sequence from Seed. Sample-accurate and the same in the JSFX, the GFX version and the VST3/CLAP.

humanize.card_desc: Random Timing, Velocity & Groove for MIDI
humanize.keywords: midi humanize humanizer random timing velocity groove swing shuffle 8ths 16ths laid back push feel drums keys quantize seed
slider_desc: How far each note may move in time (0 to 30 ms), at random, earlier or later; the plugin reports this as latency so the moves can go both ways.
How much each note's velocity may change at random (0 to 50% of its velocity), up or down.
A groove applied on top of the random moves: Straight (none), Swing 8ths or Swing 16ths (the off-beat notes later), Laid Back (every note later) or Push (every note earlier).
How strong the groove is (0 to 100%): for the swings 100% is a full triplet shuffle, for Laid Back and Push 100% is 25 ms.
The start of the random sequence (1 to 9999): the same seed gives the same moves on every playback, since it starts again at each transport start.
uses: Loosen up quantized drum programming so it sounds played
Give step-sequenced keys and pads natural velocity variation
Add swing to straight MIDI parts without editing them
A laid-back or pushing feel for a whole part
Repeatable humanization: the same seed sounds the same on every playback
humanize.properties: A MIDI effect: MIDI in, MIDI out, the audio passes through untouched (place it before an instrument). A MIDI effect cannot send a note before it arrives, so everything goes out a fixed latency later (Timing plus Push's move), reported for delay compensation; each note-on then moves by a random amount within ±Timing plus the groove's shift at its place in the beat (the host's beat while it plays, a beat at the tempo while it is stopped). A note-off follows the groove at its own place and never comes before its note-on; a pitch two notes share starts again cleanly; all notes off releases the channel's notes first; other messages keep their place, the latency later. The random numbers are an exact Park-Miller sequence from Seed, started again at every transport start. Sample-accurate and the same in the JSFX, the GFX version and the VST3/CLAP.

riff.keywords: midi riff generator melody generator pattern step sequencer random seed tempo sync arpeggio bassline lead hook key scale pentatonic blues rhythm lock accent
slider_desc: The key the riff is in.
The scale the riff's notes come from (major, minor, harmonic or melodic minor, the modes, major or minor pentatonic, blues); the key you hold starts the riff on the scale note at or below it.
Picks the riff (1 to 999): every seed is a different pattern, and the same seed always plays the same riff, in REAPER and in every DAW.
How many of the steps play a note (0 to 100%); the first step always plays, the others are rests when they miss.
The length of the pattern in steps (4 to 32) before it repeats; more steps add to the end of the same riff.
The step length, synced to the tempo: 1/8, 1/16 or 1/32 notes, or their triplets.
How far the riff climbs above the key you hold: 1 to 3 octaves of the scale.
How long each note lasts as a share of its step (10 to 100%): short values play staccato, 100% plays legato.
Keeps a rhythm while Seed rolls new notes: 0 is Off (the rhythm follows Seed); any other value plays the rhythm of that seed (the LOCK RHYTHM switch in the display sets it to the current seed).
How much the step velocities vary below the velocity of the key you hold (0% plays every step at it).
The share of steps that are accented, played well above the others (0 to 100%).
How often a step plays a new note instead of repeating the note one beat earlier (0% repeats a one-beat motif, 100% is all new notes).
uses: Hold one key and get basslines, leads or hooks that are always in key
Roll through seeds to find a riff, then lock its rhythm and change only the notes
Tempo-synced arpeggio-like runs and triplet rolls from a single held key
Transpose a riff live: the key you hold is its root, the last key pressed leads
Feed any synth or sampler with endless, repeatable melodic ideas
riff.properties: A MIDI effect: MIDI in, MIDI out, the audio passes through untouched (place it before an instrument). The pattern comes from two separate Park-Miller random streams seeded by Seed: one for the rhythm (which steps play, their velocity and accents), one for the pitches (root jumps, steps and skips, motif repeats), so it is fully deterministic and Rhythm Lock can keep one while the other changes. While the host plays, the steps sit on its beat grid (the step is the beat position divided by the rate, modulo Steps); stopped, the riff starts with the key and runs at the host's tempo. One note sounds at a time and every note-on gets its note-off; releasing every key, all notes off (CC 120/123) or the transport stopping ends the riff. Pitch bend, controllers and sustain pass through; poly pressure of the leading key goes to the note sounding. Sample-accurate and the same in the JSFX, the GFX version and the VST3/CLAP.
